title: The Phase Climb
summary: FIG. 07 makes the method one argument: four phases stand on a single baseline as the Kelwin mark's nested sequence at its true proportions, each piece ending where its strip ends, and red marks the selected phase via a Plurel control. The head echoes the hero's left stack and ties the audit to phase 01. It replaces today's subway-line stepper and boxed readout.

reference.borrowed: The margin-to-margin bar chart. Flat blocks of rising height stand on one 1px baseline, with an empty 'zero' slot at the left holding the axis caption and a value label at each block's top edge. Growth is told by height alone: no gridlines, no gradient.
reference.kelwin: The blocks became the Kelwin mark's nested sequence at the corrected master proportions: the core square (42×38), the middle L (94, bars 38/39), the outer L (152, bars 45/44) and one further step at the same ratios (216, bars 50). Bars are about 30% of each box. The drawing is not labelled as the logo. Each piece's right edge lands on its strip divider below, so figure and list share one grid. Completed phases settle into one neutral tone (--fg-3, so both skins read the same), and the selected phase is the plate's one red element. The in-block values became mono PH tags, the axis caption reads 'PHASE →', and the plate has the direction-A caption band and a Plurel segmented control in tracked caps. The head echoes the founder's hero: a red-square caps label, a two-voice statement, the 48×2 red rule and the lede stacked down the left, and a bottom-right annotation ('A system, not a project · Phase 01 is the System Audit'). Hairline strips below carry the real Methodology.tsx copy with mono OUTPUT lines.

motion: entrance: the label row fades in (300ms). The two statement lines rise out of masks (800ms --ease-out), with the light line landing 320ms after the first. The 48×2 red rule draws from the left (500ms), then the lede and the bottom-right annotation fade up 12px in turn. The plate fades in, and the four pieces rise out of the baseline one at a time as unbuilt --panel-2 ghosts (700ms each, 120ms stagger). Tags and strips follow.

state: at 1.75s red lands on Diagnose (400ms, the 'installed' beat). The control then auto-steps to Architect at 2.9s, Install at 4.0s and Calibrate at 5.1s. Each passed piece settles into the neutral done tone and red crossfades to the next piece (760ms --ease-inout). The 2px rail above the strips slides to the matching strip (900ms), and strips for unreached phases sit at 42% opacity until their turn. The sequence comes to rest on Calibrate at about 6.0s.
ambient: none. The hero film is the page's only loop.
interaction: the segments are real tabs; a click jumps to that phase and stops the demo. Hovering a strip lifts its title to --fg.
on the live site: the phases step with scroll while the plate is in view (about one phase per quarter of the section's travel). Reduced motion shows the final, fully built state.
notes: The statement is edited to 'We install the system. / Then keep it sharp.' so it fits on two lines at 96px. Coherence pass: the CTA pair was removed from this head — the red Calibrate step is the act's one red element, and the audit is still named in the annotation ('Phase 01 is the System Audit'); the doors live in the hero, fit, FAQ and final CTA. The method copy is lightly trimmed from Methodology.tsx; the outputs are verbatim. 'Phase 01 is the System Audit' follows the source's own note that the audit is step one; 'ten working days, fixed scope' is the hero's audit copy. Direction-coherence pass: A's one section rhythm is 112px top / 96px bottom in the render (160/160 on the live site); the head grammar is the hero's — Mona 500 11px tracked-caps label with an 8px red square (mono FIG. number at right), 96px two-voice statement on the display tokens with exactly one light phrase, 48×2 red rule, 20px lede in cols 1–6 (≤ 50ch, ≤ 3 lines), optional quiet door, and the founder's bottom-right annotation; FIG. numbers run 01–11 in homepage order; segmented controls are 11px tracked caps.
